title: The 10 Best Hot Glue Guns
subtitle: Mini and full-size, dual-temp and cordless hot glue guns for crafts, repairs and woodworking, ranked from live Amazon data.
intro: A hot glue gun bonds wood, fabric, foam, plastic and paper in under a minute. We ranked 10 best-sellers on rating, review volume and features (dual or adjustable temperature, full-size sticks, cordless use and sticks in the box). Mini guns take 0.27-inch (7 mm) sticks for crafts; full-size guns take 0.43-0.44-inch (11 mm) sticks and push more glue for repairs and woodworking. They run from about $10 for SHJADE's mini kit to $45 for AdTech's 200 W professional gun.
data_source: Amazon product listings on the data_captured date. Prices, ratings and review counts change daily; check the listing before relying on a number.

At 4.2 stars it's the lowest-rated glue gun we compared.

buyers_guide.a: Mini guns (0.27-inch sticks) are light and precise for crafts, cards and small repairs. Full-size guns (about 0.44-inch sticks) push much more glue, which you need for wood, larger repairs and long beads.
Low heat protects foam, fabric, ribbon and fingers. High heat bonds stronger to wood, plastic and metal. Dual-temp guns cover both.

buyers_guide.q: How many watts do I need?
buyers_guide.a: 20 W mini guns handle crafts. 60-100 W full-size guns keep up with steady gluing. 150-200 W guns are for production work and heavy repairs.

buyers_guide.q: Are cordless glue guns worth it?
buyers_guide.a: For gluing on ladders, outdoors or around a room, yes. Base-heated guns stay hot only a few minutes off the stand; battery guns run longer.

buyers_guide.q: How do I avoid burns and strings?
buyers_guide.a: Use the stand, keep fingers clear of the nozzle, and try low temperature for delicate work. Drip-free copper nozzles cut down on strings.
